alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring may be overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The patient's last creatinine was 76 umol/L on 2025-12-15 (38 days ago), which is within normal range. However, no eGFR was recorded. If the prior creatinine was also from 2025-12-15, the next 12-month TDF renal screening would fall due around December 2026. Confirm whether eGFR was calculated at the last visit, as TDF can cause chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome.

evidence.recommended_action: Verify eGFR was calculated with the December 2025 creatinine. If not, calculate eGFR now and ensure annual TDF renal monitoring schedule is documented.

alerts.title: DTG baseline glucose screening not documented
alerts.message: Guidelines require baseline random or fasting blood glucose at the time of starting or switching to DTG, as hyperglycemia has been reported in previously non-diabetic adults on DTG. The patient has been on DTG since 2022, but no blood glucose result is recorded. While the patient is stable with no reported symptoms, the absence of any documented glucose screening represents a monitoring gap. Consider checking blood glucose at the next routine visit.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform a random or fasting blood glucose test at the next routine visit to address the undocumented DTG pharmacovigilance screening requirement.
